description: Apogee Labs is a team of AI and coding enthusiasts from Kochi, Kerala. We're tackling Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, building an AI-powered crop-advisory tool that turns NASA climate and Earth observation data (rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health) into simple guidance for farmers facing changing monsoon patterns. Skills: AI/ML,  web development, data analysis and visualization, UI design. Our team is full.
summary:
Smallholder farmers in erratic monsoon regions face severe monocropping degradation, sudden rainfall deficits, and rising temperatures. Field Shift is an open-source, explainable decision support tool that transforms multi-sensor NASA Earth Observations and ground-truth soil testing into resilient 3-to-5 year crop rotation sequences. 

The platform synthesizes NASA POWER agroclimatology, SMAP surface soil moisture, GPM satellite precipitation, MODIS vegetation indices, and Landsat field-scale land surface data alongside ISRIC SoilGrids and local wet-chemistry soil assays. 

Rather than relying on ungrounded black-box AI, Field Shift enforces Stage 1 Hard Agronomic Constraints (temperature biological limits, planting windows, soil pH, and seasonal water budgets) followed by Stage 2 Transparent Linear Scoring across three distinct trade-off profiles: Balanced, Water-First, and Soil-First. An interactive "What-If" climate simulator tests farm resilience under −20% rainfall scenarios in real time, empowering smallholders and agricultural extension officers with portable, downloadable planting calendars.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Field Shift bridges satellite Earth Observations and localized smallholder agriculture through a transparent, 7-step decision workflow:

1.Field Registration & Boundary Confirmation:Smallholders verify their parcel boundary via an interactive Leaflet mapping interface with automated geodesic area calculation (pre-loaded with a 2.4-hectare benchmark farm).

2. Multi-Sensor Environmental Observation: Fetches daily and monthly solar irradiance, temperature extrema, and precipitation totals from the NASA POWER API, alongside satellite soil moisture (SMAP), precipitation estimates (GPM IMERG), and canopy vegetation trends (MODIS/Landsat).

3. Dual-Source Soil Intelligence:*Combines accredited laboratory wet-chemistry tests (pH, organic carbon %, N-P-K in kg/ha, texture, depth) with 250m ISRIC SoilGrids data, displaying explicit data-class badges ([Measured], [Observed], [Modeled], [Farmer-Entered]) and calculating calibration deltas.

4. Stage 1 (Hard Agronomic Constraints): A deterministic screening engine that screens out crops violating physiological temperature ranges, seasonal planting windows, soil pH/drainage thresholds, or water budgets.

5. Stage 2 (Explainable Multi-Year Scoring): Evaluates qualifying crops via a transparent weighted formula:

Suitability = Σ(w_i × s_i)

across Climate, Soil, Water, Season, and Rotation Fit, generating 3-to-5 year sequences across three profiles: Plan A (Balanced Resilience), Plan B (Water-First Optimization), and Plan C (Soil-First Regeneration).

6. Interactive "What-If" Climate Simulator:Allows farmers to stress-test their plan under −20% rainfall deficits, heat spikes (+1°C to +5°C), or delayed monsoons, instantly recalculating constraints to flag water-budget violations.

7. Actionable Decision & Export:Generates one-click standard .ICS planting calendars, comprehensive printable HTML/PDF agronomic audit reports, CSV telemetry datasets, and workspace JSON backups.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

- Smallholder Climate Resilience:Protects smallholders from catastrophic single-crop failures caused by erratic monsoons and dry spells.

- Soil Health Regeneration: Breaks monoculture pest cycles and rebuilds depleted soil organic carbon through biological nitrogen fixation (cowpea, groundnut) and green manure cover crops (sunn hemp).

- Zero-Cost Accessibility:Built purely on free, publicly accessible NASA Earth Observations and open-source web technologies, requiring no expensive proprietary hardware or subscription fees.

- Farmer Agency & Extension Collaboration: Includes a "Human Override" audit log ensuring local agronomic knowledge (such as canal release dates and lime amendments) takes precedence over coarse satellite grids.

What tools, coding languages, and software were used?

- Frontend & Core Engine: Vanilla JavaScript (ES2024), Semantic HTML5, CSS3 Custom Properties (zero bloated framework dependencies for ultra-fast low-bandwidth loading on rural devices).

- Spatial Mapping: Leaflet.js with OpenStreetMap cartography and surveyor-grade polygon geodesic area calculations.

- Data Analytics & Visualization: Plotly.js for multi-trace dual-axis time-series visualization (rainfall bars, temperature curves, solar radiation).

- APIs & Data Feeds: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, ISRIC SoilGrids REST API, Open-Meteo near-real-time weather feed.

- Storage & Offline Resilience: Client-side Web Storage (localStorage) and IndexedDB caching for offline field operation.

- Deployment & Hosting: Netlify Static Edge CDN.

4. How is the project creative and innovative?

- Explainability over Black-Box AI:While many modern agricultural apps use opaque generative AI that hallucinates crop recommendations, Field Shift enforces transparent, auditable agronomic rules where every score breakdown is visible and customizable via interactive sliders.

- Multi-Sensor Synthesis: Rather than relying on a single weather dataset, it synthesizes 5 NASA missions spanning optical, thermal, radar, and microwave wavelengths with ground-level laboratory chemistry.

- Uncertainty Safeguards: The platform strictly labels all simulated outputs as "Scenario Assumptions" rather than deterministic forecasts, adhering to the highest standards of scientific integrity.
